from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title and Lecture Lines
        title = "The Revelation: Emergence of the Normal Distribution"
        lines = [
            "As we collect more samples, something magical happens.",
            "The graph transforms into a smooth, symmetrical bell shape.",
            "This beautiful curve is called the Normal Distribution.",
            "It emerges regardless of the original population's messy shape.",
            "This phenomena is the famous Central Limit Theorem."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Axis positioned at row E
        axis_start = self.grid["E1"]
        axis_end = self.grid["E6"]
        axis = Line(axis_start, axis_end, color=WHITE)
        self.add(axis)
        
        # Mean dots cluster (using grid horizontal center x=3.0)
        dots = VGroup()
        for _ in range(50):
            x_offset = np.random.normal(0, 0.7)
            # Center x is at column 3.5 (midpoint of 3 and 4) which is x=3.0
            pos_x = 3.0 + x_offset
            # Clamp dots within the axis range
            pos_x = max(axis_start[0], min(axis_end[0], pos_x))
            dot = Dot(point=[pos_x, axis_start[1], 0], radius=0.04, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.6)
            dots.add(dot)
            
        self.play(FadeIn(dots, shift=UP*0.2), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Histogram bars (Cyan) - rough shape
        bar_heights = [0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 1.2, 1.4, 1.2, 0.8, 0.5, 0.2]
        bars = VGroup()
        bar_width = 0.45
        start_x = 3.0 - (len(bar_heights) * bar_width) / 2
        
        for i, h in enumerate(bar_heights):
            rect = Rectangle(
                width=bar_width - 0.05, 
                height=h, 
                fill_color="#00FFFF", 
                fill_opacity=0.6, 
                stroke_width=1
            )
            rect.move_to([start_x + i * bar_width, axis_start[1], 0], aligned_edge=DOWN)
            bars.add(rect)
            
        self.play(
            FadeOut(dots),
            Create(bars),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Smoother bars (More bars, taller)
        smooth_heights = [0.1, 0.2, 0.4, 0.7, 1.1, 1.5, 1.9, 2.1, 1.9, 1.5, 1.1, 0.7, 0.4, 0.2, 0.1]
        smooth_bars = VGroup()
        s_bar_width = 0.28
        s_start_x = 3.0 - (len(smooth_heights) * s_bar_width) / 2
        
        for i, h in enumerate(smooth_heights):
            rect = Rectangle(
                width=s_bar_width - 0.02, 
                height=h, 
                fill_color="#00FFFF", 
                fill_opacity=0.7, 
                stroke_width=0.5
            )
            rect.move_to([s_start_x + i * s_bar_width, axis_start[1], 0], aligned_edge=DOWN)
            smooth_bars.add(rect)
            
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(bars, smooth_bars),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Gold bell curve overlay
        # f(x) = peak * exp(-(x - mean)^2 / (2 * sigma^2))
        bell_curve = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: 2.2 * np.exp(-((x - 3.0)**2) / (2 * 0.9**2)),
            x_range=[0.5, 5.5],
            color="#FFD700"
        )
        # Shift the graph to the axis height
        bell_curve.shift(UP * axis_start[1])
        
        self.play(Create(bell_curve), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Pulse the bell curve in brightness (stroke width)
        self.play(
            bell_curve.animate.set_stroke(width=8, color="#FFFFFF"),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=0.8
        )
        self.play(
            bell_curve.animate.set_stroke(width=8, color="#FFFFFF"),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=0.8
        )
        self.wait(2)
